title: Phase Geometry: An introduction
description: Phase Geometry: An Introduction proposes that coherence, not continuity, is the fundamental structure of physical and cognitive reality. Where physics models systems as evolving within space and time, phase geometry describes how those very notions arise from asymmetric temporal constraints that determine what can exist, when it can exist, and how coherence is maintained. The paper distinguishes phase geometry from the geometric phase of quantum mechanics: the latter operates within established mathematics, while the former defines the conditions that make any formalism coherent. Through examples drawn from perception, sound propagation, and relativity, the work shows that reality unfolds in discrete rhythmic intervals rather than continuous evolution. Recent empirical evidence from transformer architectures reinforces this framework — their sinusoidal encodings and harmonic attention patterns reveal phase-based computation rather than symbolic reasoning. Phase geometry thus provides a unifying, empirically grounded ontology connecting physics, cognition, and machine intelligence through the shared logic of temporal coherence.
